facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with an enlarging purpuric patch on his left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
initially present for 2 weeks
the lesion first developed in March 2014 and was fairly stable until June 2014
rapid growth and extension followed by central ulceration and bleeding
a 30 × 25-cm centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
involving: Left anterior scalp with extension posteriorly on left parietal scalp
No evidence of lymphadenopathy in preauricular, cervical, occipital, submandibular or supraclavicular areas
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5
No evidence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases
Staging: T2N0M0

concepts.why: The presence of rapid growth, ulceration, and bleeding, along with the histopathological findings of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells, suggest Angiosarcoma.

The clinical presentation of a purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with the histopathological findings, could be consistent with Kaposi's Sarcoma.
The presence of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells could suggest a Hemangioma, although the clinical presentation and rapid growth are atypical.

The clinical presentation of a rapidly growing, ulcerating lesion, along with the absence of lymphadenopathy, could suggest a Lymphoma, although the histopathological findings do not support this diagnosis.

The clinical presentation of a purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, along with the histopathological findings, could be consistent with Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.

The clinical presentation of a rapidly growing, ulcerating lesion, along with the histopathological findings, could suggest Merkel cell carcinoma, although the absence of lymphadenopathy and the specific histopathological features do not strongly support this diagnosis.
The staging of T2N0M0, as indicated by the imaging studies, is consistent with a localized angiosarcoma of the scalp, which explains the enlarging purpuric patch and rapid growth of the lesion.

rationales.F07: The absence of lymphadenopathy makes lymphoma less likely.

rationales.F11: The absence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases makes lymphoma or other metastatic diseases less likely.

The specific involvement of the scalp and the staging of T2N0M0 further favor the subtype 'Angiosarcoma of the scalp'.
